content: Constipation is a potential side effect of this medication. It is important to understand that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they have determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. This medication may increase serotonin levels in the body, which, in rare cases, can lead to a serious condition known as serotonin syndrome or serotonin toxicity. The risk of developing serotonin syndrome is higher if you are also taking other medications that increase serotonin levels. Therefore, it is crucial to inform your doctor or pharmacist about all the medications you are currently taking, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements. Refer to the Drug Interactions section for more details. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Similarly, if you are in Canada, consult your doctor for guidance on side effects. Before using granisetron, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Additionally, this medication may be affected by sunlight or make the application site more sensitive to sunlight. While wearing the patch, ensure it is covered (e.g., under clothing) to prevent exposure to sunlight and artificial UV sources like sunlamps. Avoid using tanning booths. After removing the patch, keep the application site covered for an additional 10 days to protect it from sunlight. If you are scheduled for an MRI test, inform the testing personnel that you are using this patch, as some patches may contain metals that can cause serious burns during an MRI. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. The risk of serotonin syndrome or toxicity increases if you are taking other drugs that elevate serotonin levels. Examples include street drugs like MDMA (ecstasy), St. John’s wort, and certain antidepressants such as SSRIs (e.g., fluoxetine, paroxetine) and SNRIs (e.g., duloxetine, venlafaxine), among others. If someone overdoses on this medication patch, remove the patch if possible. For serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose or fail to use the patch at the correct time before your scheduled chemotherapy appointment, inform your doctor promptly. Store the patch at room temperature, away from heat. Do not open the pouch until you are ready to use the patch. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
